```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with the four package scaffolds (root `pyproject.toml`). Azure services per the ADR (status Proposed, 2026-10-05).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index catalog covering a configured range of archived quarters | §3 R1; §2.1 Backfill; §4.2 Backfill | A | 1 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (one listing, one index), so seconds at 3 req/s; byte volume measured by Stage 1. Basis: §4.2 sources, §4.8 rate |
| O2 | The catalog kept current from daily indexes, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §2.1 Daily ingestion; §4.2 Daily ingestion | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year plus listing reads per run, seconds per run at 3 req/s. Basis: one index per business day, §4.8 rate |
| O3 | Parsed, validated and normalized index rows in Parquet, each with its source provenance | §3 R3; §2.1 Metadata ETL; §4.4; §4.5 Canonical row contract; §4.6 Parse, Transform | A | 3 | Compute and memory measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Azure Monitor | §3 R4; §4.1; §4.9 | A | 4 | Dollar cost cannot be estimated without running; measured by Stage 6 (§2.2 gives no cost guarantee before measurement) |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs that share one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 One image, shared commands | A | 5 | No separate cost |
| O6 | Original index files kept, so a parser change reprocesses them without downloading again | §3 R6; §4.3 Validation before acceptance; §4.5 | A | 6 | Raw storage equals the bytes downloaded, per retained snapshot; measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of quarterly indexes that records additions and field changes | §3 R7; §2.1 Reconciliation; §4.2 Reconciliation; §4.4 | A | 7 | About 2 requests per supported quarter each week, e.g. 100 quarters ≈ 200 requests ≈ 70 s at 3 req/s. Basis: arithmetic from §4.8 |
| O8 | All SEC traffic held to one shared request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8; §4.3 One request budget | A | 8 | Caps all collection at 3 req/s (§4.8); no other cost |
| O9 | Readers get each quarter's complete current dataset through one pointer, never half-written files | §3 R9; §4.5; §4.6 Publish | A | 9 | Storage grows with each retained generation; retention is a deployment value (§4.8) |
| O10 | No record leaves the catalog without an approval tied to the exact source file | §3 R10; §4.4 Closed quarter, Changes | A | 10 | Your partner's time per approval; frequency unknown until reconciliation runs |
| O11 | Stated starting defaults for schedules, retries and request rate, validated and changed only by configuration review | §3 R11; §4.8 | A | 11 | Your partner's review time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). One track: every outcome builds on the same catalog.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly baseline on real data
      Objective: Download a small configured range of real archived quarterly indexes and turn them into a local Parquet catalog.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the four package scaffolds; an SEC User-Agent identity and a small inclusive quarter range from your partner
      Produces: shared downloader and parser; local catalog Parquet for the range; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — catalog Parquet exists for every quarter in the configured range, or each failed quarter is reported by name. O3 — every row of those quarters matches the §4.5 canonical row contract, or its source is refused with line and reason. Findings record the real run's bytes downloaded, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, requests issued and peak request rate.
      Leaves out: daily ingestion: Stage 2. Source manifest: Stage 3. Published generations behind an active pointer: Stage 4. Reconciliation and withdrawal gate: Stage 5. Azure deployment: Stage 6. Shared request budget across collectors: Stage 7. Full validation suite, scheduling and deployment, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Extend the catalog from real daily indexes from a handoff date, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader, parser and local catalog
      Produces: daily discovery with a durable boundary and pending/failed source tracking; one downloader and parser serving backfill and daily runs
      Exit: O2 — a run after a simulated multi-day gap ingests every listed daily file since the last boundary, reports `no_new_sources` on an empty listing, and leaves a failed listing's boundary unmoved. O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader, parser and output code, differing only in source selection.
      Leaves out: source manifest: Stage 3. Published generations: Stage 4. Azure deployment: Stage 6. Shared request budget: Stage 7. Scheduling and deployment: Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Retained sources and replay
      Objective: Keep content-addressed original bytes and a source manifest so outputs can be rebuilt without SEC requests.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2 collection and parsing
      Produces: source manifest (§4.5 Source, Snapshot, Workset binding, Processing, Attempt records); content-addressed raw store; immutable observation output per snapshot and parser version
      Exit: O6 — after a parser-version change, the catalog rebuilds from stored raw bytes with SEC access disabled, unchanged hashes skip work, and repeated inputs yield no duplicate logical records.
      Leaves out: published generations: Stage 4. Azure storage: Stage 6
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Generation publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as a complete generation behind one conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 source manifest and observation output
      Produces: per-quarter generations with publication manifest and change report; active-pointer resolution for readers (point-in-time reproducibility by generation id)
      Exit: O9 — with crashes injected before files finish, before the pointer update and just after it, a reader resolving the pointer sees only complete generations, and a competing publisher cannot overwrite a newer pointer.
      Leaves out: Table Storage pointer: Stage 6
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and hold any key removal for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 2 shared downloader and parser; Stage 3 manifest; Stage 4 publication
      Produces: reconciliation command; approval records; `awaiting_approval` candidate state
      Exit: O7 — a changed quarterly snapshot publishes its additions and field updates with a change report, and unchanged bytes skip transformation. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays unpublished until an approval naming its exact source hash and generation; open-quarter absence and failed responses withdraw nothing; stale daily replay cannot restore an approved withdrawal.
      Leaves out: weekly schedule: Stage 8. Approval runbook and alert: Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure platform in an isolated environment
      Objective: Run discover, collect, transform and publish as Container Apps Jobs under ADF, on ADLS and Table Storage, in an isolated environment.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 commands and contracts
      Produces: versioned infrastructure with managed identities, ADF pipelines and job definitions, all triggers disabled; manifest and pointers in Table Storage
      Exit: O4 — integration tests on isolated Azure resources pass for identities, job start and poll, conditional pointer updates and log delivery; a bounded live smoke test of one archived quarter and one published daily index, then a raw-storage replay, records byte and row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest, request rate and the environment's cost (§7 steps 3–5).
      Leaves out: shared lease-based request budget: Stage 7. Scheduling and deployment, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Shared SEC request budget
      Objective: Hold every collector to one Storage-backed lease and request budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 6 Azure Storage and job definitions
      Produces: lease-based collector coordination with daily-first turn order
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never issue overlapping requests, retries count toward the 3 req/s budget, and lease loss stops new requests until the successor's wait expires.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment: Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 8: Production backfill and scheduled operation
      Objective: Validate configuration, run the production backfill and catch-up, and enable the daily and weekly triggers.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stages 6–7; deployment values from your partner (range, handoff date, region, retention, alert recipients)
      Produces: full validation suite (historical-format golden fixtures across the chosen range, §4.6; §6 CI exit criteria); scheduling and deployment; monitoring, alerts and runbooks (§4.7, §8); release record
      Exit: O11 — every §4.8 key is validated before network I/O and a bad value is refused; the release record names image digest, configuration revision and active quarter generations; observed scheduled daily and reconciliation runs match their durable reports (§7 steps 6–9).
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list O1–O11, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Every spec requirement R1–R11 is cited by an outcome's Spec cell; list any that the accumulated system leaves unmet. Each unmet item exits as a new stage or a deferral with a written why.
```

Stages follow your ranking except where dependencies reorder them (replay and publication come before reconciliation, and Azure (O4) comes at Stage 6 after the local contracts it hosts). Do you approve this 8-stage partition, or what should change?
